tests.title: Accommodation Inquiry / University Housing Application
tests.subtitle: Section 1 — a conversation between a student, Maria, and a university housing officer about applying for university accommodation.
tests.instructions: You will hear a conversation between a student and a university housing officer. Answer questions 1-5 as you listen. The recording is played only once.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, this is the University Housing Office. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Hi, I've just been offered a place on the business course, and I need to find somewhere to live.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Congratulations. I'll just take down a few details. Can I have your name, please?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Yes, it's Maria Lopez.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And could you spell your surname?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Certainly. L-O-P-E-Z.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Now, are you looking for university accommodation, or would you prefer a private rental?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: University accommodation, please.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No problem. Do you have a preference for the type of room — a studio flat, a shared apartment, or a family house?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: I'd like a studio flat, if that's possible.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A studio flat. That's one hundred and twenty pounds per week.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Right, and are bills included in that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, water and electricity are included, but the internet is extra — that's ten pounds a month.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Okay. What facilities are available?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There's a shared laundry room on the ground floor, and residents can use the gym in the basement for free.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: That sounds good. Do I need to pay a deposit?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, a deposit of two hundred pounds is required to secure the room.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: And when can I move in?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: From the first of September. I'll email you the contract today.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you for your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. Goodbye.

tests.title: Library Membership Registration
tests.subtitle: Section 1 — a conversation between a student, Daniel, and a university librarian about registering for a library membership.
tests.instructions: You will hear a conversation between a student and a university librarian. Answer questions 1-5 as you listen. The recording is played only once.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Good afternoon, you've reached the Hillbrook University Library. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Hi, I'm a new student here and I'd like to register for a library membership.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Of course, that's no problem at all. Could I take your name, please?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Yes, it's Daniel Green.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Thank you, Daniel. And which course are you studying?

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: I'm studying environmental science.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Excellent. The membership fee is forty pounds for the full academic year.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: And does that let me borrow books straight away?

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Yes, it does. As a standard member you can borrow up to twelve books at one time.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: That's a lot. And how long can I keep them?

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Books are due back after four weeks, and you can renew them online twice before they are overdue.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Great. When does registration close?

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: Registration closes on the thirty-first of October, so you have plenty of time.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you very much.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'll send you the membership form by email today.

tests.title: Campus Tour Booking / Welcome Centre Enquiry
tests.subtitle: Section 2 — a conversation between a visitor, Emma, and a tour guide at the campus Welcome Centre about booking a place on a campus tour.
tests.instructions: You will hear a conversation between a visitor and a tour guide at the campus Welcome Centre. Answer questions 1-5 as you listen. The recording is played only once.

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: Good morning, you've reached the Riverside Campus Welcome Centre. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: Hello, I'd like to book a place on next week's campus tour, please.

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: Certainly. The tours run every weekday, so which day would suit you?

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: Next Tuesday, if that's possible.

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: Tuesday is fine. The tour starts at half past nine in the morning and lasts about two hours.

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: And how many people normally go on each tour?

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: We keep the group size to a maximum of fifteen so that everyone can hear clearly.

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: Great. And where do we meet?

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: Please meet at the main entrance, just outside the library. Your guide will be holding a blue flag.

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: Perfect. Do I need to book online before I arrive?

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: Yes, bookings close at five o'clock on the day before the tour. I'll email you a confirmation now.

transcript.speaker: Visitor
transcript.text: Thank you so much for your help.

transcript.speaker: Tour Guide
transcript.text: You're welcome. We look forward to seeing you on Tuesday.
